red: Assumptions and dependencies - the things that will move the date if they are not true
The plan covers the website only. The applications are out of scope and are listed on the BRD Out of Scope sheet.

Data layer development is done by Kestrel web dev. Twenty working days are assigned. This is the single activity most likely to move the go live date, because nothing else can be tested until it exists.
Three validation cycles on staging and one check on production. A fourth cycle would need a change request.
Kestrel QA provide a tester for each cycle. Validation with one person takes twice as long and finds less.
Staging behaves like production, including the payment gateway in test mode. A gateway that cannot fail on demand makes the payment failure solution untestable.
Test data exists for the cases that are hard to produce: a failed payment, a discount code, a null search, an order with more than ten products.
Hours for meetings and administration are not in the plan and are logged separately.
Two Workspace projects and one handover session are included. Ongoing reporting support is not.
The form component is owned by a third party with its own release window. Any change to it is outside the dates in this plan.
Consent must be answered before analytics fires. The consent tool and its categories are already live and are not being changed by this project.
